overview: NoHurtCam ships as an empty shell: the constructor registers the module and nothing else. It declares no Consumer fields, overrides no onEnable or onDisable, and toggle() therefore subscribes a handler-less instance to the event bus. The module is inert. The latent mechanism it is named for is the vanilla hurtcam: the S0B hurt-animation packet reaches NetHandlerPlayClient.handleAnimation, which calls performHurtAnimation on the local player (hurtTime 10, hurtResistantTime 20), and EntityRenderer.hurtCameraEffect turns that hurtTime into a camera offset. A real implementation would zero that offset in the render pass; the shipped class does not.

sections.p: Memeware modules get their behavior from public Consumer fields: Module.toggle() calls EventAPI.put(this) on enable, the PubSub bus subscribes the instance, and every Consumer field whose generic type matches a fired event is invoked. AntiBlind's eventConsumer0 is that pattern; NoHurtCam declares no such field and overrides neither onEnable nor onDisable, so enabling it subscribes an instance with zero handlers and disabling it removes it. The module has no settings either. Toggling it changes nothing observable, locally or on the wire.

Vanilla 1.8.9 hurtcam is receive-driven: the server broadcasts S0B (S0BPacketAnimation) with animation type 1 when the player takes damage, the fork's NetHandlerPlayClient.handleAnimation dispatches it, and performHurtAnimation sets hurtTime 10 and hurtResistantTime 20 on the local player. EntityRenderer.hurtCameraEffect (line 589) then derives the camera offset from (float)hurtTime minus partialTicks, clamping it against the 20-tick resistance window, and applies the roll and offset in renderWorld. A working NoHurtCam would either clear hurtTime each tick or replace the offset computation; this class does neither, so the camera still kicks on every hit.

The entire mechanism is client-local: S0B is server-to-client, and the camera transform happens inside EntityRenderer. Even a functional hurtcam remover would emit no packets, so the module family has no wire fingerprint. The inert shell is indistinguishable from a vanilla client by definition, and the checks below are the S0B-corpus animation-path checks that police the neighboring swing and attack traffic, none of which this module produces.

files.label: NoHurtCam.java
files.explanation: The entire shipped module: constructor plus category registration and nothing else. The absence of Consumer fields is the finding; under the Memeware event contract a module without them is a no-op.

files.label: Module.java (subscription contract)
files.explanation: The base class establishes the contract that proves inertness: toggle() subscribes the instance through EventAPI.put and the PubSub bus dispatches declared Consumer fields; NoHurtCam declares none, so nothing runs per tick. AntiBlind's eventConsumer0 is the same contract in action.

countering.label: Fight NoSwing (per-attack swing ledger)
countering.explanation: NCP's fight NoSwing enforces an arm swing between attacks: FightListener calls noSwing.check on the attack path, and a second consecutive attack with no intervening animation raises noSwingCount and the violation level, canceling at vl>2. The inert NoHurtCam neither attacks nor swings, so the ledger sees a vanilla stream and the check never engages. The entry is the honest boundary for a module with zero wire presence: the only animation-side checks that exist police the swing/attack pair, and this module produces neither side of it.

countering.label: Post (packet-order stream)
countering.explanation: Grim's Post check watches packet ordering against the movement tick stream: serverbound packets that arrive between a flying packet and its confirming transaction are queued and flagged at prediction completion, and the S0B side is onPacketSend, where a server ENTITY_ANIMATION for the player arms the swing exemption. The inert module emits nothing into the post queue and sends no C0A, so the ordering stream is identical to vanilla. The entry documents the S0B consumer that exists in Grim's tree and why a client-local camera edit cannot reach it.

countering.label: FightNoSwing (arm-swing accounting)
countering.explanation: Hawk's FightNoSwing scores ArmSwingEvent traffic: attacks that arrive without a preceding arm swing accumulate violation level with the check's decay pattern. Like every swing check it only engages when C02 attacks and C0A swings exist to mismatch. The module emits neither, so the check stays dormant. The entry is the honest statement that the swing side of the animation family cannot see a module that produces no packets at all.

countering.label: KillAura NoSwing branch (swing timer)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's KillAura NoSwing branch runs on EntityDamageByEntityEvent: when the elapsed time since the last ARM_ANIMATION packet exceeds max-swing-time (80ms by default) the check raises the NoSwing violation. The inert NoHurtCam never attacks, so no damage event is attributed to it and the swing timer never arms. The entry documents the only S0B-corpus Arc v2 check and why it is unreachable from a module whose only effect, in a hypothetical working form, would be a local camera offset.
